title: Clinical efficacy of air-polishing with and without soft tissue curettage and the adjunctive application of biologics in the non-surgical treatment of patients with peri-implantitis – a multicenter randomized controlled trial
summary:
Peri-implantitis is an inflammation of the soft and hard tissues surrounding dental implants, which is associated with bone loss and can lead to implant loss if left untreated. Plaque bacteria on the implant surface are the actual cause of the disease. The treatment of peri-implantitis primarily aims to remove the causative bacterial deposits from the contaminated implant in the peri-implant pocket. This is conventionally achieved using ultrasonic instruments and air-polishing devices. In recent years, additional measures and concepts have been discussed to improve the success of implant deep cleaning. This includes, among other things, soft tissue curettage, in which the inflamed tissue surrounding the contaminated implant is carefully and gently removed with a hand instrument. Furthermore, the use of regenerative substances to promote the restoration of lost peri-implant tissues is discussed. This also includes hyaluronic acid and enamel matrix proteins. So far, there are only insufficient data on the clinical benefit of the additional effect of soft tissue curettage and the supportive effect of regenerative substances in non-surgical peri-implantitis therapy.

The aim of this study is, therefore, to investigate whether (1) in the context of non-surgical peri-implantitis therapy, soft tissue curettage leads to better clinical outcomes compared to mechanical decontamination alone (using ultrasound and air-polishing technique), and (2) whether the adjunctive application of enamel matrix proteins or hyaluronic acid further improves the clinical outcomes.

For this purpose, 92 patients with at least one implant affected by peri-implantitis will be recruited. The patients will receive one of four different therapies at this implant, which will be assigned randomly. Therapy A includes conventional implant deep cleaning using ultrasound and an air-polishing device with trehalose powder. In Therapy B, soft tissue curettage is performed in addition to Therapy A at the affected implant. Therapy C includes, in addition to Therapy B, the application of a hyaluronic acid gel into the cleaned peri-implant pocket. In Therapy D, a gel containing enamel matrix proteins is applied into the peri-implant pocket in addition to Therapy B.

To investigate the clinical benefit of these measures, probing depths and inflammatory parameters will be measured before treatment as well as 3 and 6 months afterwards, and the changes in these values between the therapy groups will be compared and statistically analyzed.

interventions.name: Submucosal decontamination using ultrasonic and trehalose powder air-polishing (TPAP)
Submucosal decontamination using ultrasonic and trehalose powder air-polishing (TPAP) + soft tissue curettage
Submucosal decontamination using ultrasonic and trehalose powder air-polishing (TPAP) + soft tissue curettage + application of a cross-linked hyaluronic acid gel (Hyadent BG,  Regedent)
Submucosal decontamination using ultrasonic and trehalose powder air-polishing (TPAP) + soft tissue curettage + application of enamel matrix derivatives (Emdogain FL, Straumann)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Age: at least 18 years
• Patients with at least one screw-type implant with peri-implantitis (progressive bone loss of ≥3 mm; PD ≥ 6 mm, BOP and/or suppuration)
Exclusion criteria:
• Peri-implantitis therapy within the last 12 months
• Suprastructure with an emergence profile that does not allow adequate instrumentation down to the bottom of the pocket
• Insufficient mucosal thickness (visible transparency of the periodontal probe)
• Use of local or systemic antibiotics within the last 4 months
• Use of medications associated with the development of gingival overgrowth
• Use of medications that affect bone metabolism (antiresorptives)
• Systemic diseases known to interact with periodontal conditions or requiring prophylactic antibiotic coverage
• General health risk due to increased bacteremia risk
• Pregnancy
